newsitem.title: DENMARK: SAS will cuts costs without redundancies.
newsitem.headline: SAS will cuts costs without redundancies.

text.p: Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) -- which has pledged to cut costs -- said on Thursday it was not firing staff but would streamline technical operations and share more expenses with partner Lufthansa.
The airline on Tuesday published sharply lower nine-month results but said it would restore profitably through widespread cost reductions. It refuses to say by how much.
Finance Director Gunnar Reitan said savings would first be felt in the carrier's workshops.
"The earliest example will be a restructuring of SAS technical activities," he told Reuters.
"There is a potential there for improving efficiency and saving a significant amount of money," he said.
He planned no dismissals among the group's 23,000 employees, opting instead for a hiring freeze, natural wasteage, and higher productivity based on an expected rise in passenger traffic.
"General expectations for air traffic in Europe are for growth in the number of passengers in the order of five percent over the next two to three years," he said.
"That means that we can increase activity and efficiency quite considerably without laying off staff."
He also saw potential to share costs with ally Lufthansa.
At present both carriers maintained many separate overseas offices, which could be shared, Reitan said.

"That means in practice that where SAS and Lufthansa have such functions they will be merged. It will be neither SAS nor Lufthansa that close. We shall integrate some of the functions wich are today performed separately by each partner," he added.

Strengthening the alliance did not include any plans for cross-ownership, Reitan said, but a long-term goal could be to rationalise aircraft purchase so that each company could make quantity savings on spare parts. --Uffe Hansen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33 969658
